assessment.subject: cagrilintide (amylin analog) +/- semaglutide
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review argues the amylin analog cagrilintide, alone and combined with semaglutide, produces promising weight loss in clinical trials for obesity, supporting further development.

assessment.magnitude: COPD plasma GHK 70.3 vs 133.0 ng/mL; GHK-Cu raised grip strength in CS mice
assessment.subject: GHK-Cu (glycyl-histidyl-lysine copper tripeptide)
assessment.claim_summary: Plasma GHK was lower in COPD patients (n=9 vs 11 controls) and correlated with muscle measures; GHK-Cu rescued cigarette-smoke-induced skeletal muscle dysfunction in C2C12 cells and mice via a SIRT1-dependent pathway.

assessment.subject: anti-obesity medications (incretin-based and others)
assessment.claim_summary: Update review: available anti-obesity medications improve weight and metabolic parameters with variable potency, but current data do not yet support a reduction in hard cardiovascular outcomes.

assessment.subject: genetic (monogenic/syndromic) obesity treatments
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review describing current management of genetic obesity (chiefly lifestyle intervention) and emerging targeted therapies acting on the leptin-melanocortin pathway.

assessment.subject: pharmacological agents for chronic idiopathic constipation
assessment.claim_summary: AGA-ACG clinical practice guideline giving GRADE-based recommendations on pharmacological agents (fiber, laxatives, secretagogues, prucalopride) for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults.

assessment.subject: octreotide and octreotide-derived delivery systems
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of octreotide (a somatostatin analog) and octreotide-derived drug-delivery, diagnostic, therapeutic and multifunctional nanosystems in preclinical and clinical settings.

assessment.subject: liposome-anchored teriparatide (PTH 1-34) gallic-acid-gelatin hydrogel
assessment.claim_summary: Preclinical study: an injectable liposome-anchored teriparatide hydrogel gave controlled, sustained PTH(1-34) release, promoted chondrocyte proliferation via PI3K/AKT, and protected cartilage in a mouse osteoarthritis model.

assessment.subject: elamipretide
assessment.claim_summary: Phase-3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (N=218): elamipretide 40 mg/d for 24 weeks did not improve 6-minute walk distance or fatigue vs placebo, missing both primary endpoints (Class I negative evidence).

assessment.subject: CagriSema (cagrilintide 2.4 mg + semaglutide 2.4 mg)
assessment.claim_summary: 32-week phase-2 double-blind active-controlled RCT (n=92) in type 2 diabetes: CagriSema lowered HbA1c and gave greater weight loss (-15.6%) than semaglutide or cagrilintide; HbA1c reduction beat cagrilintide but not semaglutide (p=0.075).

assessment.subject: central melanocortin system / melanocortin-receptor peptides
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of the melanocortin system as a therapeutic target, noting FDA-approved peptides (setmelanotide, bremelanotide, afamelanotide) and reviewing progress and challenges in melanocortin-receptor drug development.

assessment.magnitude: -24.2% weight at 48 wk (12 mg) vs -2.1% placebo
assessment.subject: retatrutide (LY3437943, GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Phase-2 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (N=338): 48 weeks of retatrutide produced dose-dependent weight loss up to -24.2% (12 mg) vs -2.1% placebo, with mostly mild-to-moderate GI adverse events.

assessment.magnitude: HbA1c up to -2.02%; weight up to -16.94% at 36 wk; p<0.0001 vs placebo
assessment.subject: retatrutide (GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Phase-2 double-blind placebo- and active-controlled RCT (N=281): retatrutide dose-dependently lowered HbA1c (up to -2.02%) and bodyweight (up to -16.94% at 36 wk), significantly greater than placebo (p<0.0001).

assessment.subject: GLP-1 receptor agonist prescription/use
assessment.claim_summary: Retrospective database cohort: GLP-1 receptor agonist use rose sharply in University of California Health from 2014-2022 (e.g., Ozempic users 569 in 2019 to 22,891 in 2022), with similar trends across T2D, CVD and obesity subgroups.

assessment.subject: chronic constipation management (laxatives, secretagogues, prokinetics, etc.)
assessment.claim_summary: Comprehensive narrative review of chronic constipation management, describing lifestyle/dietary measures and drug classes (osmotic/stimulant laxatives, secretagogues, prokinetics); usefulness of biofeedback stated as undetermined.

assessment.subject: 'Ozempic face' (semaglutide-associated facial volume loss)
assessment.claim_summary: Dermatology commentary demystifying the social-media term 'Ozempic face', discussing whether rapid facial volume loss is a novel adverse effect or a consequence of weight loss and how clinicians should counsel patients.

assessment.subject: GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, liraglutide)
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review for emergency clinicians: GLP-1 agonists improve glucose control and weight but are associated with adverse events (GI effects, pancreatitis, biliary disease, hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, renal events).

assessment.subject: tryptathionine and 2,2'-bis-indole stapled peptides (Melanotan-II, alpha-MSH)
assessment.claim_summary: Synthetic chemistry study: a 5-hydroxypyrroloindoline condensation forms tryptathionine or bis-indole peptide staples; applied to alpha-MSH/Melanotan-II, the stapled peptides showed nanomolar and one sub-nanomolar Ki.

assessment.magnitude: tirzepatide HbA1c MD -2.10%; CagriSema weight -14.03 kg
assessment.subject: GLP-1 receptor agonists (15 drugs)
assessment.claim_summary: Systematic review and network meta-analysis (76 RCTs, 39,246 participants): all 15 GLP-1RAs lowered HbA1c and fasting glucose; tirzepatide had the largest HbA1c reduction (-2.10%) and CagriSema the greatest weight loss (-14.03 kg); GI adverse events flagged.

assessment.magnitude: semaglutide ~15-17% weight loss; tirzepatide up to 22.5%
assessment.subject: entero-pancreatic hormone-based obesity therapies (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon/amylin)
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of current and pipeline obesity drugs, citing semaglutide 2.4 mg (~15-17% weight loss), tirzepatide (up to 22.5% in phase-3 trials), and emerging combinations (CagriSema, retatrutide).

assessment.subject: amylin and analogs (pramlintide, cagrilintide)
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review summarizing the mechanism, clinical pharmacology and applications of amylin and its analogs (pramlintide, cagrilintide) for glucose homeostasis, satiety and weight in diabetes and obesity.

assessment.subject: tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Drug review: in phase-3 SURPASS trials once-weekly tirzepatide was superior to dulaglutide 0.75 mg, semaglutide 1 mg and insulin for glycaemic control and weight loss in T2DM, and was generally well tolerated (mainly GI adverse events).

assessment.subject: obesity treatments in primary care (lifestyle, AOMs, surgery)
assessment.claim_summary: Review of obesity management in primary care: lifestyle interventions yield ~2-9% weight loss at 1 year with common regain, whereas highly effective antiobesity medications induce mean weight loss of 15% or more.
